title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling, Benchmarks, Runbooks, and Release Notes
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview

This consolidated reference covers the Redwood Serving Runtime: architecture overview, kernel selection and scheduling rules, profiling/playbook procedures, benchmarking suite and interpretation of results, release notes for the 2027-Q4 runtime release, known issues and mitigations, and operational runbooks used by the runtime team. The goal is to provide a single, actionable page for engineers and SREs to understand design trade-offs, run diagnostics, and perform safe rollouts.

1) High-level runtime architecture

Summary:
- Purpose: high-throughput, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Core components: request router, model worker pool, kernel selection layer, KV cache manager, batching/dispatcher, telemetry hooks, and the control plane for rollouts and routing policies.

Architecture diagram (textual):
- API -> Router -> Policy engine -> Worker pool (GPU pods) -> Kernel runtime -> HW (NVIDIA A100/H100, AMD MI250, Intel Gaudi2)
- Sidecars: metrics exporter, trace injector, sec-agent (for Private/VPC).

Key design constraints and invariants:
- Stateless request routing for scale; model state (KV cache) lives on worker instance and is recoverable via checkpointed warm-starts.
- Default SLOs: p50 token latency <= 8ms, p95 token latency <= 28ms for 8k context on H100 in dedicated tier; throughput targets published per instance type in the Model Catalog.
- Safety: any kernel that triggers >2x baseline OOMs in the test harness is rejected from production.

2) Kernel selection & scheduling rules

Purpose: select best-performing kernel path given model architecture, quantization profile, sequence length distribution, and target latency/cost trade-off.

Priority order for kernel selection (simplified):
1. Verified hardware-accelerated kernel (architecture + device match)
2. Quantization-aware kernel (int8/4) if model profile marked supported
3. Fallback optimized CPU kernel for cold-starts or small workloads

Selection heuristics and thresholds:
- If median seq_len >= 2048 and model has attention-optimizations, prefer kernel-A (attention-fused) on H100.
- If memory headroom < 1.2x (measured by runtime reservation), prefer kv-segmentation + offload to host for non-high-priority traffic.
- If observed p95 latency > target and batching_utilization < 60%, increase batch window by +5ms up to +25ms; if p95 still > target, fallback to lower-quantized kernel with quality regression guard.

Kernel blacklist/whitelist rules:
- Blacklist kernels flagged as unstable in the last 7 days across >=2 clusters.
- Whitelist experimental kernels only in canary and dedicated-dev tiers.

3) Profiling playbook (how to run a diagnostic)

This playbook helps reproduce and diagnose performance regressions and memory anomalies. Follow the steps below in order.

Pre-reqs:
- Access to runtime staging cluster (role: runtime-debugger).
- Profiling image: gcr.redwood-inference/runtime-profiler:2027-11.
- Bench dataset: workloads/prod-synthetic-8k-2027-10.tar.gz.

Procedure:
1. Reproduce the issue with the production request trace: capture a trace for a 5-minute window (use trace-id from incident).
2. Run the perf harness in staging using the same request mix:

   ```bash
   ./bench/run_harness.sh --config configs/harness/prod-mix-8k.yaml --workers 8 --duration 300
   ```

3. Attach profiler to a worker pod:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/<worker-pod> -- /bin/bash -c "/opt/profiler/profile --output /tmp/profile.pb"
   kubectl cp serving/<worker-pod>:/tmp/profile.pb ./profile.pb
   tensorprof view profile.pb
   ```

4. Metrics to examine:
- GPU util, SM active cycles, memory allocs, memcpy times (host<>device), kernel launch latency, and all-reduce durations.
- Runtime-level: batch waiting time, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, quantization-dequantize overhead.

5. If kernel launch latency spikes >30ms with low GPU util (<40%), suspect driver/kernel mismatch or PCIe contention. Check dmesg and nvidia-smi topo -m.

6. If memory fragmentation observed (many small allocations), consider enabling pool allocator flag: --allocator=arena and re-run harness.

4) Benchmarking suite and interpreting results

Benchmark components:
- micro-bench: kernel-level latency & memory (per op)
- macro-bench: end-to-end token latency for standard prompts and chat workloads
- stress-bench: long-running throughput test with churn and mixed sequence lengths

How to run full suite (CI):
- CI pipeline name: runtime/perf/full-suite.
- Command (example):

   ```bash
   make bench-full TARGET=H100 CONFIG=8k-parrot WORKERS=16 DURATION=900
   ```

Interpreting results (examples):
| Metric | Baseline (H100) | Current | Action threshold | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p50 token latency | 6.2ms | 8.1ms | >+20% | Kernel regression or scheduling inefficiency |
| p95 token latency | 24ms | 35ms | >+30% | High-variance workloads, profiler required |
| throughput (tokens/s per GPU) | 2200 | 2000 | <-10% | Check batch window and GPU util |
| KV cache hit ratio | 0.78 | 0.44 | <-20% abs | Caching misconfiguration or routing to cold workers |

Bench result gating rules:
- Any candidate kernel or runtime change that increases p95 by >15% or reduces throughput by >12% must be blocked from auto-promotion; require perf-owner signoff.

5) 2027-Q4 release notes (runtime v3.12.0)

Summary of user-visible changes:
- New kernel-A v2.3 with attention fusion and reduced memory footprint on H100/H100S: up to 18% p50 improvement on long sequences.
- Quantization pipeline updated: int8 symmetric fallback for GPT-style models with reduced dequant latency (-10%).
- Improved batching dispatcher: adaptive windowing for long-tail requests.
- New telemetry: per-kernel latency histogram, and kv-cache eviction counters.

Behavioral changes and rollout plan:
- Default kernel for seq_len>4k switched to kernel-A v2.3 in canary on 2027-11-05 and staged rollout to 10%/30%/100% over 3 weeks.
- Quality guard: if model eval regression >0.7% deviation on downstream eval set during canary, auto-rollback will trigger.

Upgrade notes for Dedicated/Private customers:
- For on-prem upgrades, minimum driver versions required: NVIDIA 22.12.1 or later; CUDA 12.2. See upgrade checklist below.

Upgrade checklist (ordered):
1. Ensure backup of /var/lib/runtime/checkpoints and config repo.
2. Validate driver versions (nvidia-smi --query).
3. Deploy canary worker group (label: canary=v3.12.0).
4. Run bench-full against canary group and validate gating rules.
5. Gradual rollout and monitor SLOs for 72 hours.

6) Known issues and mitigation

List (short):
- ISSUE-2027-451: kernel-A v2.3 on AMD MI250 may see fallback hangs on mixed-precision workloads. Mitigation: pin kernel to kernel-B for MI250 or upgrade driver to 5.4+.
- ISSUE-2027-463: KV cache eviction race under heavy shard churn causing elevated cold misses. Mitigation: enable kv-coordinator=true in config and increase eviction_backoff_ms to 200.
- ISSUE-2027-478: Profiling agent may fail on private air-gapped installs due to missing CA bundle. Mitigation: install ca-certificates package or use offline profiling image.

7) Runtime runbooks (operations)

Runbook: High p95 token latency (incident triage)
1. Validate scope: check Grafana dashboard: runtime/token-latency by model, by pod. Confirm p95 > SLO for >5m.
2. Check recent deployments: kubectl rollout status on serving deployments in last 30m.
3. If rollout detected, rollback to previous revision and monitor.
4. If no rollout, run profiling playbook (see section 3).
5. Escalation: page runtime-oncall -> if root cause not resolved within 30 minutes, page infra-oncall and ModelOps.

Runbook: Worker OOMs or frequent restarts
1. Check pod events: kubectl describe pod <worker-pod>. Look for OOMKilled.
2. If OOMKilled, retrieve /var/log/runtime/oom.log and recent profiler snapshot.
3. If OOM pattern correlates to kernel change, de-register kernel via runtime-admin --kernel-unregister <kernel-id>.
4. Increase reserved memory by 10% for the worker pool as a short-term mitigation.

Runbook: KV cache thrash leading to throughput drop
1. Verify KV hit ratio in dashboards. If <50% and traffic unchanged, check shard mapping changes in control-plane logs.
2. Activate kv-coordinator and rehydrate caches from last checkpoint: runtime-ctl kv rehydrate --shard <id> --from-checkpoint <ts>.
3. If rehydration fails, route affected traffic to dedicated cold-worker pool and continue rehydrate.

9) Configs and examples

Sample runtime config (YAML):
| key | example | description |
|---|---|---|
| kernel_preference | ["kernel-A","kernel-B"] | Ordered list of kernel ids to try |
| allocator | "arena" | Memory allocator used by runtime |
| kv_coordinator | true | Enable centralized KV rehydration coordinator |
| eviction_backoff_ms | 200 | Milliseconds backoff on repeated evictions |

Inline YAML snippet:

```yaml
runtime:
  kernel_preference:
    - kernel-A
    - kernel-B
  allocator: arena
  kv_coordinator: true
  eviction_backoff_ms: 200
  telemetry:
    publish_per_kernel_histograms: true
```

10) Team wiki & housekeeping
- This document is the canonical runtime reference and is reviewed monthly by the runtime triage meeting.
- Add any new kernel experiments to the wiki page: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-experiments and include bench artifact links and perf diffs.
- Archive older release notes under /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes-archive.

Appendix: Debugging quick commands
- Check pod-level GPU metrics: kubectl top pod -n serving --containers
- Dump last 5 minutes of runtime logs with timestamps: kubectl -n serving logs deployment/worker --since=5m --timestamps
- Force canary to 0% if immediate rollback is required: runtime-ctl rollout adjust --deployment worker --stage canary --percent 0
